author: Daisy Rathi
text:
You’re definitely not alone severe adhesive reactions are unfortunately very common, especially in kids with sensitive skin. We went through the same cycle of inflammation, oozing, and sensors falling off early. It’s exhausting.

Many families have had success with a hydrocolloid barrier (cutting a hole for the filament), or using barrier films like Cavilon instead of Skin Tac, which can actually worsen reactions for some kids. Rotating sites aggressively and giving the skin full breaks is also key.

One thing that helped us was finding ways to reduce the pressure to “push” sensors longer than the skin could tolerate. Using BluCon NightRider, we were able to get continuous glucose data and remote alerts even when sensors couldn’t stay on as long, which took a lot of stress off both us and our child especially overnight.
